newsitem.title: ITALY: Union leader tells Italy govt to agree global plan.
newsitem.headline: Union leader tells Italy govt to agree global plan.

text.p: Coalition parties backing Prime Minister Romano Prodi should agree on a global pact covering 1997 and 1998 budgets, as well as a reform of the welfare state, the leader of Italy's largest union federation said.
"This pact should cover the period of time between now and the end of 1998," Sergio Cofferati told Corriere della Sera newspaper.
Cofferati signalled on Saturday that his Cgil union was open to suggestions for changes to social spending, but told Corriere that it would be a difficult problem to resolve.

"Discussions on the welfare state...will take months," he predicted, adding that any reform of the pensions system would have to respect the 1995 reforms introduced by the then prime minister Lamberto Dini.
Post and Telecommunications Minister Antonio Maccanico said on Monday he was in favour of working with coalition partners on a far-reaching plan covering government spending.
Analysts have urged Prodi's centre-left government to hack back at the welfare state, especially costly state pensions.

Prodi is due to unveil a mini-budget later this week with up to 16 trillion lire of deficit cutting measures, but government ally Communist Refoundation has already vetoed any cuts to pension or health spending. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
